sourceEvidence.label: WireScope privacy threat model and artifact writers

assessment.summary: Sensitive artifact creation is dispersed across recorders and can be consolidated behind an owner-only file boundary.

assumptions: No measured latency or memory budget was supplied.
Local multi-user confidentiality is in scope.

opportunities.title: Own the private artifact boundary
opportunities.summary: Make owner-only creation and safe replacement an invariant of one output API.
opportunities.diagnosis: Sensitive files are created independently by multiple modules, leaving access mode and path policy to ambient process state and caller discipline.

evidence.claim: WireScope artifacts can contain credentials and personal network metadata.
Multiple recorders and exporters create output with ordinary file primitives and no shared permission policy.
Opt-in raw data increases the consequence of ambient file permissions.

desiredInvariants: Every WireScope-created artifact is owner-only from initial creation onward.
Sensitive writers reject unexpected final-component symlinks.
One-shot replacement is atomic where practical.
External writers are verified against the same policy.

options.title: Local file-mode guards
options.summary: Add explicit owner-only creation and checks to every current writer.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Owner-only modes reduce local disclosure but do not change sharing behavior.
Every known write site receives the direct guard.
Raw artifacts become owner-only, while explicit opt-in remains required.

tradeoffs.assessment: Known artifacts become owner-only, but future writers can omit the guard.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Create every artifact under umask 000 and inspect modes.

tradeoffs.assessment: Only per-file metadata operations are added.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare representative recording throughput before and after.

tradeoffs.assessment: No retained buffers or processes are introduced.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run representative recordings and compare peak RSS.

tradeoffs.assessment: Current write topology remains; mode failures add explicit error paths.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise writable, read-only, and overwrite destinations.

tradeoffs.assessment: No deployment component is added, but audits remain dispersed.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Search all output primitives during review.

tradeoffs.assessment: Small edits preserve formats and CLI behavior.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run current tests and new permission cases.

residualRisks: Future output paths can omit the guard.
Symlink and atomicity policy may remain inconsistent.

workPackages: Apply private creation and mode verification at every writer.
acceptanceCriteria: Every generated artifact is mode 0600 under umask 000.
migrationNotes: Preserve existing overwrite and append semantics.

options.title: Central secure-artifact API
options.summary: Consolidate file creation, streaming, replacement, and verification behind one owned boundary.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The owned boundary enforces local confidentiality; sharing warnings remain.
Current writers migrate to one policy owner while guards remain during rollout.
Raw data uses the same private sink; explicit opt-in remains necessary.

tradeoffs.assessment: The sink owns owner-only modes, symlink policy, and verification, reducing future drift.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test all writer classes under permissive umask and symlink substitution.

tradeoffs.assessment: Metadata checks and atomic rename occur per artifact, not per event.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare event throughput and artifact completion latency on representative sessions.

tradeoffs.assessment: Only bounded path and temporary-file state is added.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare peak RSS for streaming and one-shot outputs.

tradeoffs.assessment: Atomic one-shot replacement reduces partial files, though migration adds new error cases.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Interrupt writes and exercise cleanup, overwrite, and disk-error cases.

tradeoffs.assessment: One boundary and test suite replace repeated security review at each sink.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Add a static search/check preventing unapproved direct writers.

tradeoffs.assessment: One-shot, streaming, append, and external-tool outputs require separate adapters and compatibility tests.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Migrate by writer class with per-caller rollback.

residualRisks: Owner-level malware and administrators can still read files.
Stdout and deliberately shared copies remain outside the file boundary.

workPackages: Define and test the API contract.
Migrate one-shot, streaming, and external writers incrementally.
acceptanceCriteria: All artifact types are mode 0600 from creation.
migrationNotes: Preserve file formats, paths, append behavior, and CLI syntax.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Retain protected local writers until each migrated caller is validated.

opportunities.recommendation: Use a central secure-artifact API, introduced incrementally with local owner-only guards during migration.

openQuestions: Are symlinked output destinations intentionally supported?
Should explicitly shareable reports use a separate permission override?
Must proxy logs append to existing files?
